text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The European Union (EU) will only provide free crop packs to small scale Zimbabwean farmers who did not reap good harvests last season because of drought, waterlogging or other natural disasters, the EU's agricultural advisor Artur Runge-Metzger said at the weekend.

- All Southern African Development Community (SADC) member states are supporting a proposal by Zimbabwe, Botswana and Namibia for the three to be allowed to trade in ivory and other elephant products, Zimbabwe deputy minister of environment and tourism Edward Chindori-Chininga said at the weekend.
- Zimbabwe's trade promotion body, Zimtrade, has over the last few years generated over Z$40 million worth of orders for local firms from Zambian companies.
